gateway: isolated temporary home, approval=reads; a freshly seeded gateway for the stub screenshots, one for the live ones and one for the walkthrough
data: fictional, seeded through the app's HTTP API (capture/scenes.json)

agent_backend.stub: Kiro Crew's offline stub ACP backend (capture/stub_backend.py) for every other scene; no chat reply is shown from it
agent_backend.credit_reading: the browser answers the top bar's credit readout (/api/sessions/usage) with "no reading", so no account balance or email can be shown

note: The isolated gateway served this repository's own copy of the app: setup installed it from this checkout (POST /api/apps/install), trusted it and enabled it, and every picture shows its committed bundle (ui/dist/index.mjs) and backend. Kiro Crew still ships a built-in aws-control and refuses a second install under the same name, so the Kiro Crew tree the capture ran on is the commit the tests pin with only the built-in copy removed (src/kiro_crew/apps/builtins/aws_control and its BUILTIN_NAMES row); kirocrew_tree_dirty records that. AWS was a local stand-in: the gateway's AWS CLI pointed at a moto server on loopback (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL) and at a fictional AWS config with three demo profiles, so every account id, bucket, file and figure shown is fictional and no request reached AWS.
data_notes: The two accounts carry the AWS documentation's example account ids, minted in the local stand-in; the lab-sso profile's sign-in portal is an example.com address and never signs in, which is why it shows reconnect guidance.
The stand-in has no billing data, so the Usage pane's spend reads zero.
Dates are the capture day's, stamped by the gateway's clock.
